title: A connection to the landscape
excerpt: Where architecture exists in a close conversation with the landscape, materials are chosen not simply for how they look inside a house, but for how they relate to the colours, textures and feel of the environment beyond it…

blocks.text: Mountain Retreat. Image by Patrick Reynolds

Where architecture exists in a close conversation with the landscape, materials are chosen not simply for how they look inside a house, but for how they relate to the colours, textures and feel of the environment beyond it.
The Queenstown Lakes landscape is defined by contrasts: blue lakes against schist and scree, pale tussock against dark mountain slopes, and the changing light of an alpine environment.

For architects designing homes in this setting, the relationship between building and landscape is often central to the design. Materials are carefully selected to sit alongside, rather than compete with, the natural environment. Inside these homes, Ambitec polished plaster plays this role. Its colour, texture and variation provide a way to bring the qualities of the landscape into the interior, while working alongside the stone, timber and concrete commonly used in the region.
Mountain Retreat – Lake Wakatipu
Mountain Retreat - featuring a two-tone Suave poilshed plaster. Image by Patrick Reynolds

Mountain Retreat is a small structure set within a high country station over Lake Wakatipu, Central Otago. The colours and textures of the cladding integrate the building into the gravel tracks, exposed rock faces and scree slopes of the alpine environment.

Reflecting the heavily rendered stone walls, Ambitec Suave polished plaster in a two-tone combination of Tilt Slab Light and Tilt Slab Dark brings a timeless concrete aesthetic to the ceiling. Together with the stacked windows, contributing to the light open space, and connection with the outer environment.
Homestead Bay House – Homestead Bay
Nestled amongst tussock grass, Homestead Bay House overlooks Lake Wakatipu. Image by Simon Devitt

Inspired by the rugged landscape of Homestead Bay, Ambitec SuaveStone polished plaster in Stone White brings a natural texture and depth to the interior of Homestead Bay House. Its subtle soft grey tonal variation with clay and flecks of aggregate, echoes the surrounding schist and stone.

Used throughout, the finish provides continuity across the interior while complementing the home's palette of natural stone and timber. The result is a cohesive, grounded aesthetic that feels intrinsically linked to the Queenstown landscape.
Homestead Bay House - Image by Simon Devitt.
Mooney Residence – Arrowtown
Rendered stone sits in harmony with timber and Ambitec polished plaster. Image by Studio Studio
Suave in Gravel White. Image by Studio Studio

In the Wakatipu basin, an area highly characterised by luxury lifestyle properties, and historic stone walls, is Mooney Road. Approached by the architects as a “regeneration, not just a renovation” of a heritage building, one of the key details to the response was to address the ‘material tension’. Use of Ambitec Suave eased the contrast of the heavy rendered stone walls.
Suave in Illusion brings light into the common areas, while the soft brown-grey of Gravel White adds a sense of warmth and calm to the master bedroom.
Polished plaster walls, and natural materials work together to soften the home’s robust bones, allowing the old and new to sit more naturally alongside one another.
Explore more Queenstown Lakes homes
Lake Ridge House – Wanaka
Lake Ridge House. Image by Biddi Rowley
Kānuka House – Kānuka Valley
Kānuka Bay House. Image by Mickey Ross
Local materials and Ambitec polished plaster

Concrete
Concrete brings weight, strength and simplicity to a building. Its smooth or textured surfaces can be echoed in the subtle variation of polished plaster, while differences in tone and finish create interest between the two materials.

Stone
Stone brings the textures and colours of the landscape into a building, from the subtle variation of weathered schist to the sharper edges and reflective surfaces of more highly finished stone. Ambitec polished plaster can complement these qualities through its own tonal variation and tactile surface, providing either a quiet contrast or a continuation of the stone's natural palette.

Timber
Timber introduces warmth and a sense of organic detail, whether through polished flooring, exposed beams, or the grain and texture of more rustic finishes. Against these surfaces, polished plaster can provide a softer, more restrained plane, allowing the natural variation of the timber to remain prominent.

Across the Queenstown Lakes, these materials take on different forms, shaped by the architecture, the setting and the preferences of the people who live in these homes. Ambitec polished plaster offers another surface to work with: one that can sit quietly alongside stone, timber and concrete, or introduce a contrasting texture and tone.

The result is not simply a connection between materials, but a relationship between the interior and its setting. Through colour, texture and the way light moves across a surface, polished plaster can help carry something of the surrounding landscape into the spaces we inhabit.

title: An architect working with Ambitec
excerpt: Ambitec polished plaster has been specified by architects across a range of residential projects, from new builds and major renovations to their own homes. What draws them to it is the ability to develop the finish around the architecture — refining colour, texture and polish to work with the materi

blocks.text: When an architect specifies a material once, it can be a matter of circumstance. When they return to it across multiple projects, and ultimately choose it for their own home, it says something more.

Ambitec polished plaster has been specified by architects across a range of residential projects, from new builds and major renovations to their own homes. What draws them to it is the ability to develop the finish around the architecture - refining colour, texture and polish to work with the materials, light and atmosphere of each space.
Master Bedroom - Wawata House, designed by architect Julian Guthrie for his family. Image by Simon Devitt.

Architect Julian Guthrie has worked with Ambitec across several residential projects, including Pacific House, Pauanui Beach House and Dune House. He chose Ambitec polished plaster again for Wawata, his own family home on Waiheke Island.

For architects, specifying materials for their own homes is perhaps the greatest endorsement, and Ambitec polished plaster continues to be the finish of choice for those seeking exceptional texture, craftsmanship and longevity.
A material to work with, not simply specify

Polished plaster offers architects an opportunity to consider the wall as a material in its own right, rather than simply as a surface to be painted. Its colour, texture and degree of polish can be developed alongside timber, stone, concrete, metalwork and other materials within the scheme.

Julian describes Ambitec’s approach as artisan, with custom samples and an interior-only focus. This allows the finish to be explored and refined before it reaches the wall, taking into account how colour, texture, polish, natural light and neighbouring materials will work together.
Julian works with Jill Goacher of Intext Design to select Ambitec colours, ensuring they work with the complete material palette.
“We love the custom combinations of both colours and textures, and giving walls character and texture.”
Pauanui House - featuring a two-tone Suave poilshed plaster. Image by Simon Devitt
Dune House - featuring SuaveStone polished plaster. Image by Ambitec
Wawata: Choosing Ambitec for home

There is a difference between specifying a material for a client and choosing to live with it yourself. At home, the finish is experienced every day — through changing light, alongside furniture and other materials, and simply as part of daily life.

At Wawata House, Julian worked closely with Ambitec to develop a finish that complemented the home's palette of concrete, timber and stone. Used throughout the upper-level entrance, bedrooms and bathroom, the plaster adds subtle depth and texture without competing with the architecture.
“We love the subtle colour and textural depth, which changes with varying light conditions and works well with all the other materials in the house.”
Living with the material has also given Julian a perspective beyond its appearance. He describes the finish as “easy to live with and hard wearing too, relative to a plain painted wall.”
Entrance - Wawata House, designed by architect Julian Guthrie for his family. Image by Simon Devitt.
Different architecture, different expression
The projects where Ambitec polished plaster have been specified are not defined by a single aesthetic.

Julian's work demonstrates this particularly clearly. Pacific House combines board-formed concrete, extensive glazing, limestone and bleached oak. Pauanui Beach House retains its original concrete structure alongside oiled cedar, while Dune House combines Moroccan limestone, oiled cedar, corten steel and blue.
Wawata takes a different direction again, bringing concrete, timber and stone together within a home designed around its coastal setting.

Across these projects, Ambitec polished plaster has been adapted to the architecture rather than imposing a predetermined style. The finish can be quiet and restrained, or more expressive, depending on the combination of colour, texture and polish developed for the space. Collaboration from specification to installation.

The quality of a finished plaster surface depends on more than the material itself. Preparation, application and finishing all contribute to the result, making the relationship between the design team and installer an important part of the process.
Beach views and Soft Suave walls feature in Pacific House. Image by Ambitec
Clerestory window and Ambitec Suave walls feature in Pacific House. Image by Ambitec
More than a finish

For architects, the appeal of Ambitec polished plaster goes beyond what is applied to the wall. It is the opportunity to develop a finish alongside the architecture, refine it through sampling, and see how it evolves once it becomes part of a lived space.

Julian Guthrie's decision to work with Ambitec in his own family home speaks to that relationship. These are not simply materials specified for clients, but finishes chosen to be lived with every day.
Perhaps that is the real measure of a finish: not simply how it looks when a project is photographed, but how it performs as part of the architecture and how it feels to live with over time.

title: Custom colours for polished plaster
excerpt: Learn how Ambitec matches custom colours for polished plaster, and how product, texture, polish and lighting affect the final colour and finish.

blocks.text: Colour is an important consideration when specifying polished plaster. Unlike paint, where colour is applied as a uniform surface coating, the colour of polished plaster interacts with the texture, polish and natural variation of the material. Light also affects how the colour is perceived, meaning the same colour can appear quite different depending on the finish and environment.
Ambitec offers a range of standard colours across our plaster products, as well as a bespoke colour matching service for projects requiring a specific colour.
Custom finishes at Tax Traders, designed by Material Creative, who used our custom colour service. Image by Samuel Hartnett.
How colour behaves in polished plaster

Colour in polished plaster is experienced differently from paint. Rather than sitting on the surface, the subtle movement within the finish allows light to interact with the material, giving colour a richness and depth that changes throughout the day.

The degree of polishing also affects the appearance of colour. A higher level of polish can increase the depth and intensity of the colour, while a more textured finish produces greater variation across the surface. When a dark colour is combined with a higher level of polish and a penetrating sealer, the result can be a particularly rich and deep appearance.
Texture, polish and light

Light reveals texture
Texture affects the way light moves across the surface. More pronounced textures create greater variation between areas of light and shade, while smoother finishes provide a more consistent reflection of light.

Consider the space
In brightly lit spaces, the relationship between colour and texture becomes particularly important. A darker colour with a medium texture, or a combination of two tones, can provide depth without creating excessive visual contrast.

Consider the lighting
Natural light changes throughout the day according to the orientation of the room, windows and skylights. Artificial lighting also affects the appearance of the finished surface. The position and direction of fittings, colour temperature and localised sources such as wall sconces, LED lighting and fireplaces can all influence how colour and texture are perceived.
Custom Mauve two-tone at The InterContinental Auckland by Warren & Mahoney. Image by Jono Parker.
Custom finish - Lonely Grey at Lonely Wellington by Knight Associates. Image by Simon Wilson
Choosing a custom colour
If you're looking for a colour beyond our standard ranges, Ambitec offers a bespoke colour matching service.
To order a custom colour sample:

Provide a reference
Please provide us with a brush out or drawdown of your paint colour that you are wanting to match or a sample of your tile or wallpaper if something specific from your project’s material palette.

Select the plaster
Let us know which plaster product you want customised - Suave, SuaveStone or SuaveCrete.

Select the finish
Specify the polish and texture level - A standard medium texture and polish will produce a different appearance from a more highly polished finish. The level of polish can affect the way the colour is perceived, so the sample should reflect the finish intended for the project.
How Ambitec matches custom colours

Ambitec's colour matching is carried out by eye, adjusting individual pigments through a series of iterations to achieve the desired tone. Because the colour changes as the plaster dries and is sanded, each version needs to go through the same process before the final colour can be assessed.
Archival library → visual matching → iterations → drying/sanding → final sample
Allow time for custom sampling

This means colour matching cannot be rushed. Several iterations may be required, and each sample needs time to dry before it can be sanded and assessed. For this reason, please allow at least 2–3 weeks for custom colour matching and sampling.

title: Understanding substrate preparation for polished plaster
excerpt: A practical guide to polished plaster substrate preparation. Learn how Level 4 finishes, detailing, and coordination impact final results.

blocks.text: To achieve the expressive finishes of polished plaster requires attention to detail when prepping your surface. Like any wall finish, the final result comes down to the substrate beneath it. This is no different from paint or wall coverings. Good preparation leads to a good outcome.

From a construction point of view, preparing a surface for polished plaster is not more difficult than preparing for paint. In most cases, a standard Level 4 finish, flat, dry, and free of visible defects, is all that is required. The confusion usually comes from the word “plaster”. It is often assumed that it will behave like a stoping compound and correct imperfections in the wall. That is not the case.

Polished plaster is a thin decorative finish, usually around 1 to 1.5mm. It is not designed to fill gaps, level surfaces, or correct poor workmanship. If the substrate is not finished properly, those issues will remain visible.
Polished plaster does not require a higher standard than paint. It simply relies on the substrate being finished correctly.
Substrate preparation: comparable to paint
Polished plaster is applied over surfaces that meet a Level 4 plasterboard finish.
In practical terms, this means:
Boards are properly installed and stopped as per manufacturers requirements
Surfaces are smooth and even
The wall is clean, dry, and ready for finishing
Walls also need to be straight and stable, within standard tolerances, and free from movement in the lining. These are standard requirements for any quality paint finish.
Where detailing really matters
The main difference with polished plaster is not just the wall preparation. It is the level of attention needed in the detailing.
Because the finish is thin, it will follow the surface exactly as it is.

All penetrations need to be in the right place and the right size before work begins. If changes are made later, the repair will be visible. Matching a polished surface is similar to matching a natural material such as timber.
Polished plaster will not:
Fill gaps left around power points or plumbing
Hide oversized holes
Disguise patching
Edges and junctions also need to be clean and sharp, free from excess stopping compound and ready for masking.
Any build-up of compound around joinery, skirting, or tiles needs to be removed before finishing. The plaster will follow what is already there. It will not correct untidy edges.
Early coordination reduces risk
Polished plaster outcomes are often influenced by decisions made early in the project.
Engaging with the plaster system and installation requirements during the design and planning stage helps ensure that:
Substrate specifications are clearly defined
Junctions and material transitions are properly detailed
Penetrations and set-outs are coordinated before lining begins
Where these considerations are addressed early, the risk of rework is reduced and a more consistent result can be achieved.
Why architects and designers choose polished plaster

Polished plaster is often specified as an alternative to paint in high-end projects. It offers depth and movement to the surface, helping to read more consistently across large areas or in difficult lighting conditions.
It is commonly used when:
Walls are exposed to strong natural or directional light
A Level 5 paint finish is difficult to achieve consistently
A more refined, material-driven finish is desired
For designers, this gives more control over how a space feels and looks once complete.
What this means in practice

Polished plaster is not a more difficult finish than paint, but it does behave differently. It relies on the work that comes before it rather than correcting it. As a thin-applied finish, it will follow the substrate exactly as it is presented. It will not fill gaps, straighten edges, or resolve poor set-outs.

When the substrate is properly prepared to a consistent Level 4 standard and the detailing is accurate, polished plaster provides a reliable and high-quality result. It can also offer a more controlled visual outcome in spaces where paint finishes are harder to manage, such as large wall areas or surfaces exposed to strong natural light.

For builders and designers, the takeaway is simple. Treat polished plaster like any other premium finish. Get the basics right, pay attention to the details that matter, and install it at the right stage of the build. When those elements are in place, polished plaster becomes a practical and effective way to achieve a refined architectural finish.
You can read more about substrate recommendations on our FAQ page or give us a call if you need further support.

title: Certified installers & nationwide coverage: How Ambitec supports consistent design across New Zealand
excerpt: Ensure consistent polished plaster finishes across New Zealand with Ambitec’s certified installer network. Supporting architects and designers with reliable, high-quality outcomes nationwide.

blocks.text: Specifying a polished plaster or architectural wall finish is only one part of the process. How those materials are applied has a direct impact on how they appear in the finished space.

Small variations in pressure, timing, or technique during installation can subtly influence the tone, texture, and reflectivity of a surface. For architects and designers, this means the success of your specification depends heavily on the skill of the installer.
Leaving the final outcome to interpretation introduces a level of risk that no project can afford. So, how can you minimise that risk and ensure the finished result matches your design intent?

A simple and effective approach is to require a final sample panel in the specified colour, texture, and finish. Ideally, this should be produced in a 600 × 600 mm format (or a sample wall on larger projects), then reviewed and signed off by all project stakeholders. This ensures alignment before installation begins and allows adjustments to be made early, avoiding costly rework later.
Rambler bar in the Drifter Hotel by Claddagh Plastering in Christchurch
Why installation defines the outcome

Unlike uniform coatings, polished plaster is applied by hand. Each pass of the trowel contributes to the character of the surface, and even small differences in technique can result in visible variation.
This makes installation an integral part of the overall design process, not just a finishing step.

To ensure consistency, Ambitec works with a certified network of plaster applicators across New Zealand. These installers are trained in specific Ambitec systems and finishes, with a deep understanding of how surfaces behave under different lighting conditions and within varied spatial contexts.
Through this network, architects and designers can specify with confidence, knowing their design intent will be delivered consistently, regardless of the installer or project location.
Supporting architects and designers nationwide
For practices delivering projects across multiple regions, the challenge is not only sourcing an installer; but ensuring consistent outcomes from one site to another.

Ambitec’s certified installer network addresses this by ensuring all approved applicators are trained to deliver the full range of Ambitec finishes. Rather than reinterpreting specifications on every project, installers operate from a shared technical framework and application standard.
This reduces variability, minimises on-site corrections, and ensures continuity across projects.

Whether your project is based in Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch, or Queenstown, finishes can be replicated with precision, maintaining their intended aesthetic and material quality across different environments.
Upper Watt Street by Overcomer Applicators in Wellington
Lake Ridge House by Dowd Concrete & Plaster in Queenstown
A consistent approach, no matter the project
Beyond geographic reach, the real value of a certified installer network lies in technical alignment and shared expertise.

Every installer works from the same product systems, application methods, and performance expectations. This consistency reduces reliance on on-site interpretation and allows designers to focus on broader spatial and material decisions.

Where required, Ambitec also provides technical support, ensuring finishes are suited to project-specific conditions. This may include guidance on substrate preparation, environmental factors, or how surfaces will respond to natural and artificial lighting.
Explore Ambitec’s certified installer network

As demand for high-end plaster finishes continues to grow, Ambitec is expanding its nationwide certified installer network throughout 2026. The focus remains on strengthening regional capability while maintaining strict standards of quality and consistency.
For architects and designers, this means greater access to skilled, trusted applicators, regardless of project location.
Get in touch to discuss your next project wherever in New Zealand it might be.

title: Supporting the next wave of artists at the Aotearoa Art Fair 2026 Ambitec
excerpt: Ambitec proudly supports William Austin Gallery and Kurutai Collective at the Aotearoa Art Fair 2026, creating custom textured wall panels and rendered plinths that deepen the experience of contemporary and Māori uku art.

blocks.text: The Aotearoa Art Fair has always been a place where ideas, materials, and creative voices converge, and this year, we’re proud to be a supporting partner, helping to realise the vision of the next wave of gallerists and artists, both new and established, exhibiting at the Fair for the first time.
Both galleries highlight the breadth of contemporary practice in Aotearoa, from intergenerational painting to uku (clay) works grounded in whakapapa and place.
Not only presenting raw and real works, they are also challenging the status quo of how art is traditionally shown, bringing new meaning and power to the connection between space and art.

Our contribution sits quietly within this shift: crafting soft textured finishes for the wall panels and custom plinths that ground each presentation in materiality. These elements help the work feel immediate, lived‑in, and deeply connected to the kinds of spaces where art is actually experienced.
William Austin Gallery
First up, William Austin Gallery from Wellington, who will be presenting historical and new paintings by Hariata Ropata‑Tangahoe, alongside works by Julian Hooper, Anna Sisson, and Rangi White.
A thoughtful, intergenerational presentation that brings together distinct voices in contemporary art, each exploring form, symbolism, and storytelling in their own way.
To further support and add another dimension to how the works are experienced, we are creating soft textured wall panels, a subtle backdrop while adding depth and material presence to the booth.
Hariata Ropata Tangahoe
Julian Hooper
Anna Sisson
Rangi White
Kurutai Collective

We’re equally proud to be supporting Kurutai Collective, curated by Chantel Matthews, who will be showcasing new works by Dorothy Waetford and Graham Tipene, alongside an incredible group of emerging and established Māori uku artists.

To realise Chantel’s vision of a ‘space of convergence where the synergies of iwi, artists and ideas meet, mix and inter-flow with Māori creativity and culture’, we are creating custom rendered plinths, designed to complement the clay works and evoke the flow of ‘kurutai’ brackish water ( where waitī, fresh water and waitā, (salt water mix), through form and materiality.
Graham Tipene & Dorothy Waetford at Auckland Studio Potters
Amanda Kemp
Fleur Palmer
Commitment to collaboration

We’re honoured to play a small part in supporting these artists and their stories. This project reflects what drives us at Ambitec: thoughtful collaboration, material sensitivity, and a commitment to the creative communities that shape Aotearoa’s cultural landscape.
Our involvement builds on previous partnerships, including our work with Knight Associates and McCahon House, where materiality played a central role in shaping the visitor experience.
Come see these incredible galleries, artists and more inspiring work at Aotearoa Art Fair in Auckland from April 30th - 3rd May.

title: Our first NZ Design Week event, Aotearoa Made: A new era of colour and craft
excerpt: NZ Design Week included the launch of Ambitec’s new Auckland showroom, a space celebrating the tactile beauty of our architectural polished plaster finishes.

blocks.text: On Thursday, 5 March, we had the privilege of hosting our first New Zealand Design Week partner event, Aotearoa Made: A New Era of Colour and Craft , a celebration of people, place, and the power of making.

It was also our opportunity to share a few exciting milestones in our commitment to sustainably and locally produced architectural finishes, brought to life in a space designed to hold that conversation.
Unveiling the new Ambitec showroom
The event was held in our new Auckland showroom, an endeavour which has allowed us to demonstrate the breadth of the Ambitec brand in a way that samples and swatches simply can’t.

Bold in colour, rich in texture, and grounded in craft, we continue to expand the range of bespoke interior finishes available for architects and designers in New Zealand. And now, within our new Mt Roskill premises, visitors can explore each of our polished plaster finishes, experiencing how light and texture interweave to influence the way a space is perceived.
Throughout the evening we offered an intimate look into the Ambitec story; the why behind what we do, the thinking and making that shape our work, and the partnerships that continue to guide us.

The event also marked the soft launch of our nearly-ready, locally manufactured polished plaster finishes. For us, it very much felt like both a celebration of how far we’ve come, and a new beginning.
Honouring craft and collaboration

We had the pleasure of showcasing a collection of artworks by David Austin and Tristan Marler, part of a wider collective of Māori uku/clay artists curated by Chantel Matthews of Wai Create. We’re proud to support their journey to the 2026 Aotearoa Art Fair,creating the plinths for their booth as part of our ongoing collaboration.

Their work is a reminder that craft is more than technique; it is connection, identity, and story. Their pieces sat beautifully within the showroom because they reflect the same values that guide us: people, place, and the power of the handmade.
Conversations about craft and colour

At the opening of our showroom, we strived to do much more than simply enjoy good company and share our new space. Instead, we wanted to open a conversation about craft, colour, the role of imperfection in artistry, and the way materials shape the human experience.

Be it art or architectural finishes, any handmade surface is rarely static. It shifts with light, responds to its surroundings, and reveals more to you the longer you spend with it. Colour has a huge influence in this, but how it’s realised depends on the hands and decisions involved at every stage.
Plaster may be a traditional surface, but at Ambitec, our products allow the creatively inclined to explore their vision and for the craftsman to create something exceptional.
For that reason, Ambitec has always been a collaboration between designers, installers, makers, and clients, and this next chapter is no different.
Looking toward an exciting 2026

As we continue to refine our Aotearoa-made polished plaster finishes, we’re excited for what comes next. We’re continuing to explore new textures, new colours, and new opportunities to walk the intersection of craft and contemporary design.
If you’d like to experience the space or learn more about our locally made finishes, we welcome you to visit our Auckland showroom or explore our work at ambitec.co.nz.

title: Lighting and texture: Enhancing interiors with polished plaster finishes
excerpt: Polished plaster has become a familiar presence in architectural spaces, though its success relies on more than surface appearance alone.

blocks.text: Polished plaster has become a familiar presence in architectural spaces, though its success relies on more than surface appearance alone. Light and its orientation can be determining factors in how the finish is read. This in combination with the colour, texture and polish level must be considered simultaneously when samples are prepared for approval.
In New Zealand architecture, where light can shift dramatically from one hour to the next, that’s a point not to overlook.

Polished plaster with a smooth texture and high polish tends to give off an even reflection, while textured surfaces introduce shadow and variation. Subtle differences in tone won’t be picked up in full sunlight, but become more apparent under filtered or indirect light. By understanding how lighting, colour and texture interplay, designers can specify finishes that are successful from the sample boards to the finished walls.

Two of our recent projects, Westmere House and the Fisher & Paykel Auckland Experience Centre, are great examples of how materials from the same family can be tuned to suit entirely different high-end interiors.
Low light lifestyle on a south-facing site, Westmere House

Westmere House sits on a steep, south-facing site that descends from the street, forming layers of living throughout. With low natural light, polished plaster was used as dramatic focal points in curated areas of the home.

Instead of using the wall material to brighten, the vision was for it to carry depth and warmth as natural daylight diminished. Ambitec’s Suave polished plaster was specified with a medium texture and polish in Beautiful Black, allowing depth to develop as daylight diminished. The surface absorbs light rather than reflecting it, which allows the texture to register as light washes across the space.
Consistency and control, Fisher & Paykel Experience Centre

The Fisher & Paykel Auckland Experience Centre relies on artificial light rather than natural light to showcase its products. Here, lighting is carefully controlled and designed to guide visitors through a sequence of immersive zones. Spaces feature commercial, cultural and sculptural moments, all of which need to be complemented without competing for focus.

For this project, the wall finish would need to perform consistently under varied lighting. Ambitec SuaveCrete in Beautiful Black was chosen, with its heavy-textured properties enhanced further by the inclusion of black sand aggregate. The heavier texture introduces depth, while a low-grade polish was used to limit glare under directional and spot lighting. Texture is ever-present, but as a backdrop that adds to the atmosphere rather than demanding attention.
Designing with context in mind

As these past projects show, polished plasters may be similar in name, but they can be vastly different in nature. In one case, the plaster’s texture softens and absorbs daylight; in the other, it adds depth and substance under artificial light. Architectural wall finishes with polished plaster can give you ultimate flexibility to create your vision.
For support specifying architectural finishes, begin by exploring our technical guidance or connect with our team to discuss your project.

title: Polished plaster in commercial interiors: Enhancing brand identity with surface finishes
excerpt: Explore how polished plaster finishes can enhance brand identity and connection in commercial interiors, offering high-end, sustainable solutions.

blocks.text: In today’s design-conscious commercial spaces, every surface speaks, and walls are no exception. Whether it’s a corporate office, a luxury apartment development or a premium brand showroom, the materials you choose contribute directly to how clients, customers and stakeholders experience your brand.
Increasingly, polished plaster finishes are emerging as a refined alternative to paint or wallpaper, offering both visual impact and subtle tactility.
At Ambitec, we specialise in creating handcrafted polished plaster wall finishes that elevate interior environments and express brand identity through surface finish, tone, and timeless design.
Why surface finish matters in branding

When someone steps into your space, their first impression is formed in seconds. And it’s not just about layout or lighting – it’s the finishes they see and feel. The right surface finish can evoke warmth, refinement, heritage or innovation, depending on how it’s designed and applied.
For example:
In a corporate reception, a soft textured polished plaster finish can create a sleek, understated sense of permanence and professionalism.
In a high-end apartment lobby, a more rugged stone-like or concrete finish can create a sense of heritage or architectural grounding.
In a premium showroom, a refined decorative plaster finish might enhance the visual impact of a brand’s curated product range.
Ultimately, surface finish makes a statement – not just about how a space looks, but how it feels to be there.
Suave
SuaveCrete
SuaveStone
Bone China
Expressive finishes for commercial interiors
Not all finishes are created equal.

Ours are all built from the same core materials but can be refined, textured, tinted, or polished to suit a wide range of contexts – all while offering the durability and performance commercial interiors demand.
Our signature looks include:
Suave – a contemporary minimal finish with natural depth in colour and movement
SuaveStone – an earthy plaster finish with clay and fine aggregate
SuaveCrete – a durable, gritty, decorative plaster finish
Bone China – a delicate porcelain-like finish with fine ‘crazing’ and a pearly lustre
Because Ambitec finishes are applied by hand, they’re as unique as your brand – never off-the-shelf, and always design-led.
Explore our commercial projects to see our finishes in-situ.
Customisation and brand alignment

A key advantage of working with Ambitec is our collaborative process. No two finishes are the same – and they shouldn’t be. We work closely with designers, architects and business owners to ensure each surface complements your brand’s identity and spatial goals.
That might mean:
Developing a custom tone to align with your brand colour palette
Creating finishes that sit beautifully alongside timber, stone, metal, or glass
Designing a feature wall that reflects the tone and values of your business – be it calm and considered or bold and enduring
Whether you’re leaning into minimalism, biophilic influence, or architectural plaster aesthetics, our finishes help tell your story.
Built for commercial performance
Ambitec finishes aren’t just beautiful – they’re designed for real-world application. In high-traffic commercial spaces, durability and easy care are essential.
Our surfaces are low-maintenance and long-lasting – ideal for corporate and public-facing settings
Many finishes can be made resistant to moisture and wear with the application of a clear sealer
Finishes can be cleaned easily without compromising their visual integrity
Download our product spec sheets for more technical information.
A real-world example
Take the Fisher & Paykel Experience Centre.

title: Polished plaster maintenance: Tips from the experts
excerpt: Expert tips on maintaining polished plaster walls, ensuring lasting elegance and high-end finishes for architectural interiors across New Zealand.

blocks.text: Polished plaster is one of the few interior finishes that rewards both close inspection and long-term use. Hand-applied by skilled artisans, it brings natural texture, tonal depth, and a quiet sense of luxury to residential and commercial interiors alike.
But while these surfaces are built to last, they’re not invincible. The secret to maintaining their elegance is simple: thoughtful care and the occasional expert check-in.

At Ambitec, we believe great design doesn’t stop once the plaster dries. This guide brings together our expert advice on preserving the integrity of your walls, so they continue to reflect your space, style and standards for years to come.
Why care matters

Polished plaster isn’t precious, but it is particular. Like timber or natural stone, it will hold up beautifully when respected and maintained with intention. Routine care not only prevents premature wear, it helps preserve the subtle tonal shifts and handcrafted qualities that make each surface unique.
In high-traffic commercial spaces, a well-maintained finish is part of the customer experience. In private interiors, it’s part of the everyday joy of living with natural materials.
High-touch maintenance
In high-traffic commercial settings (reception counters; apartment lobbies) or busy home spaces like hallways and entranceways, some wear is inevitable.
Here’s how to address it:
Gently rub scuffs with a damp cloth in a circlar motion; avoid scrubbing
For light scratches gently scuff in a circular motion with a 320Grit paper (avoid if sealed)
For larger scratches or repairs contact Ambitec for expert touch-up guidance or to book in a visit
We’re always happy to advise. Often, minor issues can be resolved quickly – or prevented altogether with the right approach.
Everyday maintenance
The good news is that daily upkeep is uncomplicated. Most polished plaster finishes can be kept looking their best with minimal effort:
Dust regularly with a soft microfibre cloth to maintain a clean, even surface
For light marks, a damp cloth and water will usually suffice
Avoid abrasive sponges or harsh cleaning agents, which can compromise the finish
Where needed, use a pH-neutral cleaner, applied sparingly and spot-tested in an inconspicuous area
Like the finish itself, the right care approach is subtle and considered.
Design for durability
A few simple precautions can extend the life of your finish without compromising aesthetics:
Incorporate skirting details to mitigate wear and tear from vacuuming and mopping
In busy public settings, consider design-led deterrents like feature shelving or integrated signage that subtly redirects touch
Include dado wall panelling, stone or timber panelling along the lower high-touch sections of your wall
Use felt pads or buffers on furniture that comes into contact with walls
As with all good design, it’s about balance – protecting the finish while letting it live in the space naturally.
Commercial vs. residential: a slightly different rhythm
While the care fundamentals are the same, commercial spaces benefit from a more proactive approach – regular inspections, occasional resealing, and early intervention in high-touch zones.

In residential settings, maintenance is usually lighter. A gentle cleaning routine and a few simple habits (like avoiding contact from furniture or bags) are enough to preserve the finish for years to come.
Whether your space is public-facing or private, we can advise on a care plan that fits the pace of your environment
Resealing, refreshing, and long-term support
Over time, your polished plaster may naturally evolve – deepening in tone, softening in sheen, or developing subtle surface character. These changes are part of the beauty of natural finishes.
Still, if your surface begins to feel tired or overworked, our team can assist with:
Professional resealing to renew protection
Sheen restoration for polished finishes
Re-blending or partial resurfacing in high-contact areas
As every Ambitec finish is handcrafted, every solution is custom. We treat your wall not as a product, but as part of your architecture – and your story.
An ongoing partnership in surface design
Great finishes are an investment – in texture, in atmosphere, and in experience. They deserve aftercare that’s as thoughtful as their application.
At Ambitec, we’re proud to be more than makers. We’re long-term collaborators in the life of your space, offering guidance, technical support, and creative solutions well beyond installation day.
For personalised advice or to book a maintenance consultation, get in touch with us here, or download our Care Guide for more details.

title: How to choose the right polished plaster finish for your space
excerpt: Expert guidance on selecting the right polished plaster finish for walls, combining style, durability, and architectural appeal across New Zealand.

blocks.text: Polished plaster is fast becoming the go-to choice for architects, interior designers and discerning homeowners who want to bring depth, texture and timeless elegance to their spaces. From softly mottled tones to playful textured surfaces, this architectural wall finish offers a refined alternative to traditional paint or wallpaper.

At Ambitec, we specialise in handcrafted polished plaster finishes, where every surface is uniquely tailored and no two finishes are ever the same. Whether you're designing a serene living area or a statement commercial space, here’s how to choose the right polished plaster for your project.
Understand the space first

The right plaster finish starts with understanding how the space will be used and experienced. Is it a restful bedroom, a bold entranceway, or a moisture-prone bathroom? Is it flooded with natural light or lit primarily with downlights?
Soft textured finishes work beautifully in bedrooms or private living areas, lending a calming, cocooned feel – especially when used in combination with wall lights.
Highly reflective polished plaster can brighten spaces by bouncing light from its surface, where highly textured finishes can work well in spaces with too much light.

Joinery items or wet areas like bathrooms require the application of a clear sealer to help protect from moisture and aid in cleaning. The sealer will deepen the colour and can reduce the movement, therefore a little more texture – especially on lighter colours – will be beneficial in these more dimly lit spaces.
Download our Care Guide for practical planning tips.
Choose the right texture and tone
Polished plaster is known for its versatility – from smooth, mirror-like finishes to textured plaster that mimics natural stone, concrete, or even porcelain.

At Ambitec, we offer a wide range of decorative plaster finishes, each crafted with depth, tactility and character. It’s important to decide if the plaster finish will be the feature in the room, or if it’s intended to sit quietly in the background.
Want a stonelike or rustic, earthy look? Explore our SuaveStone or SuaveCrete ranges.
After something more refined? A Suave or Bone China finish may be the right fit.
For something more dramatic, explore deeper tones or contrasting textures – our team can guide you through options that complement your concept.
Think about colour and customisation

Colour plays a powerful role in how a space feels. Whether you're aiming for warm neutrals, moody charcoals, or clean whites, we work with you to find a tone that complements your material palette, light source and architectural features. When a project requires it, we can also develop a custom colour or two-tone combination unique to your space.
Explore our Colour Library to get inspired.
Why choose Ambitec finishes?

When you choose Ambitec, you’re choosing more than a finish – you’re choosing craftsmanship, collaboration, and care. From initial concept to application, our team partners closely with architects, designers, and homeowners to bring your vision to life.
Our finishes are designed to endure, both aesthetically and practically, with an emphasis on quality and connection – making every project deeply personal.

title: Enhance depth and movement with polished plaster
excerpt: Discover how Suave Two-Tone polished plaster creates contemporary, rich-toned finishes for high-end architectural interiors across New Zealand.

blocks.text: Suave two-tone finishes explained

Suave two-tone combines the silkiness of the Suave plaster in two shades to create a cloudy or marbled look that adds extra movement to the plaster finish. Typically applied in a light and dark shade of a similar colour to create a subtle shift, however any two-colour combinations can be applied to create a bespoke look.
Suave two-tone in a combination of ‘Greenhithe’ and ‘Pale Grey Half’ at Island Bay House.

Two-tone applications are great for spaces where the light source is limited or too bright to pick up the texture, therefore the shift in tone adds another level of movement to the surface. Also, a great option for rendered ceilings to achieve more impact, or spaces that can afford more drama.

A truly hand-crafted finish, each combination is unique and will differ through how the colours work together, the number of folds and the ratio of one colour to another. The cloudy look is achieved through the folding of the two equal portions of coloured plaster on the hawk – 4 or more folds depending on the level of blending – that creates either a muted shift (10 folds) or a more dramatic marbled look (4 folds) adding extra movement and depth to the polished finish.
Suave two-tone in a combination of ‘Misty White Double’ and ‘Tilt Slab Light’ at Red Beach House.

Able to be expressed in both our traditional and mottled applications, the two-tone finish is also a great way to achieve a concrete look, with our Tilt Slab Light and Tilt Slab Dark combination in a traditional texture, similar to a soft poured concrete. When applied in a mottled finish, the dark colour is applied first, with the lighter colour rolled over and then floated to reveal the dark tones underneath. Depending on the time of floating, this can either create a watercolour or leather effect.

Through the combination of a warm and cool tone, a soft chalky appearance reminiscent of a French or Italian villa can be achieved offering a tonal shift that provides flexibility within all colour palettes.

When specifying a two-tone finish, two colours must be selected – these can be any two colours within our range, including half or double shades. When applied in the mottled texture, thought must be given to what colour is dominant.
Suave two-tone in Tilt Slab Dark and Tilt Slab Light creates a concrete effect on the ceiling at this Villa Extension.
Suave mottled in a two-tone combination
Suave two-tone with no folding
As this is a bespoke finish, we always recommend having a sample made up to visualise your desired combination if we do not have an example in stock.

title: Ambitec polished plaster finishes on fireplaces
excerpt: Guide to using Ambitec polished plaster finishes on fireplaces, adding style, warmth, and architectural appeal for designers and architects in New Zealand.

blocks.text: Ambitec polished plasters are often specified on fireplaces as an alternative finish to paint to give the fireplace focus, substance and help ground the space.
Ambitec Suave in ‘Grey Grey’ was rendered on the fireplace in this bungalow renovation by Sayes Jackson Architects.

Before specifiying our finishes in this type of installation, it is important to understand the limitations and the safety standards that are required to be met for your build. As per our Branz Fire Certificates our Ambitec Suave, SuaveStone and Bone China polished plaster finishes meet the Building code Group 1S Classification for application on plasterboard via the NZBC Verification Method C/VM2 Appendix A and Group 3 on MDF.
The Interact panel in a large corrugate texture was used on the top section of this Ponsonby Villa fireplace, with the base in Suave Beautiful Black.

Along with understanding the group rating required, Ambitec polished plasters are suitable for use on a fireplace under the following conditions; A fire rated substrate is installed as per regulations, eg, Eterpan, Villaboard or Supalux are installed as per the manufacturers specification. All joints and corners are stopped to a level 4. (This applies to Ambitec polished plaster finishes that are applied on the vertical faces adjacent to the fire only).

Assumption is made that the finish is not returned into the firebox opening and the rising heat is deflected by a firebox surround or mantle when a tv is installed directly above. As a rule, if the fire cannot ‘see’ the Ambitec polished plaster, it is safe to use in this type of installation.
Suave in Imperial brown makes a dramatic statement in the master fireplace at Cliff House by Bosley Architects and Sonia Cotter Design.

Although our finishes can be wiped clean with a damp cloth, it is also important to note if installing a wood burner, there may be smoke residue that escapes when the door is opened during use that may cause some discolouration on the plaster over time, in particular if a lighter finish has been selected. This can be remedied by specifying a darker colour and following our Care & Maintenance guide.

Stone will always be a more durable finish on your hearth but if Ambitec polished plaster finishes are specified we recommend applying several coats of our clear sealer for added protection. (We do not recommend using Ambitec finishes on hearths with wood fires)
